Under the boundary law, with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\), the lower-endpoint projection of the band at \(y_0\) has diameter at least \(1-e\). The analogous assertion holds for the upper-endpoint projection when the class contains a boundary law with \(F_P(y_0)=0\) and alternatives with the same propensity and \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=\delta_n\), under the same \(n\)-sample total-variation condition. Such alternatives exist within the bow-SCM class whenever \(n\delta_n\to0\). Consequently, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\) cannot yield a nonconservative shrinking band uniformly over such a total-variation-local tie-inclusive class; derivative-aware inference is restricted to strata separated from these contacts, with \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) retained as the honest fallback.
